A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAM research. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, support comparison. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAM results on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, component and hyperparameter experiments, inference timings, and a 15-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds latent-space diagnostics, leave-one-out ablations, and measurements of REG’s behavior and computational cost.

M1.justification: The two-stream architecture, encoders, diffusion decoder, four training objectives, gradient control, and combined REG/CFG inference procedure remain unchanged. Reformatted equations and expanded explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-motion generation on HumanML3D and KIT-ML and retain the same user-study coverage. The added diagnostics reuse existing coverage. No noisy-data or targeted long-horizon evaluation is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds MotionDiffuse, MotionLCM v2, and COME to the HumanML3D comparison. The original MotionLCM remains separately listed, so its v2 counterpart is an addition rather than a rename. KIT-ML, user-study, and existing latent-strategy comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce joint t-SNE and paired-cosine measurements, leave-one-out controls, per-step timing at batch size 32, and a REG correction probe with B=128 and a step-5 scatter plot. Existing training budgets, sampling schedules, benchmark metrics, batch-1 AITS measurement, and user-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F substantially extend mechanism analysis: Figure 5 examines text/motion latent geometry, Table 10 tests component complementarity by removing components from full RAM, and Figure 6 examines sample-dependent REG corrections and correction magnitudes across steps. Appendix B also adds per-step overhead analysis. Earlier ablations and sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly reports a median Pearson correlation, and Figure 6(b) introduces shaded bands. The median’s aggregation and the bands’ statistical meaning are unspecified. Existing tables retain their ± reporting; neither version supplies explicit repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the original nine tables are retained. Added results include three baselines’ scores, paired cosine similarities of 0.157/0.493/0.579, leave-one-out FIDs of 0.424/0.064/0.132, REG correlation approximately 0.62, and baseline/CFG/REG/combined timing ratios of 1:1.95:2.18:3.13. These extend supporting results without changing RAM’s reported benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and guidance equations are equivalent across versions; some equation lines are combined and renumbered. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new empirical diagnostics introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: motion-centric reconstruction supervision, self-regularization and alignment, REG-based error mitigation, and state-of-the-art motion generation. The headline HumanML3D claim remains FID 0.032 and R-Precision@1 56.1% with 20 inference steps.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new diagnostics as evidence of motion-structure preservation, component complementarity, and error-adaptive REG correction. Its conclusion replaces v1’s high-quality-capture-data caveat and proposed noisy-data evaluation with a single-token conditioning limitation and plans for finer-grained, long-horizon generation.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project URL for the promised code release, without establishing that code is available. v1’s Data Availability section and direct dataset links are removed. Appendix D expands the description of existing comparison controls; it does not establish changed training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to MotionLCM v2, COME, EasyTune, FrankenMotion, and ReAlign. It removes the structured-control discussion with four associated works and four video-reconstruction/data references tied to the old conclusion. The central positioning against two-stream, VQ-VAE, and diffusion-guidance approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: the user study, inference-efficiency discussion, hyperparameter analysis, and latent-strategy implementation details move into Appendices A–D. The main text gains shorter summaries and cross-references. Related work and the conclusion are edited, Data Availability is removed, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: v2 changes page format, typography, running headers, and table-caption placement throughout. Existing displays are relocated and renumbered, Table 1 gains comparator rows, and Figures 5–6 and Table 10 are added. The qualitative motion examples and user-study chart are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The stronger comparator coverage in Table 1 and new latent-space, component, REG, and timing analyses provide additional support and cost transparency for the unchanged method. The gain is limited: the REG analysis uses an error proxy, its statistical reporting is incompletely specified, and v2 removes direct dataset links and the earlier noisy-data qualification. Overall, the added evidence modestly strengthens an already extensively evaluated paper.
